text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Cheil Jedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd on Wednesday bought 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Marubeni Corp. Shipment was set for April 10-May 10.
CORN AND SOYBEAN SALE - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp bought 24,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 6,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans from Mitsui & Co Ltd Wednesday for April arrival.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group will expand Thursday's tender to 109,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and corn, doubling its initial plan for a 54,500-tonne tender, traders said. Shipment includes 38,500 tonnes of No.2 soybeans and 16,000 of No.2 corn, traders said.

CORN, RICE, CORN/SOY BLEND TENDER - Results are expected Thursday on CCC's tender for 32,380 tonnes U.S. corn, rice and corn/soy blend for North Korea. It seeks 5,000 tonnes of corn-soy blend, 20,780 yellow corn and 6,600 milled rice. Delivery was for April 1.
CORN TENDER - South Korean feed milling companies seek 50,000 tonnes of Chinese corn for arrival in May, trade sources said on Wednesday.
- Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group will tender on Thursday for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn for April shipment, traders said.
SOYMEAL TENDER - Results were awaited on a tender by South Korean companies for 30,000 tonnes of soymeal for arrival by May 30, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - Results were awaited on Mexico's tender Wednesday for 29,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat, 13.5 percent protein, for April shipment, U.S. exporters said. It seeks 20,000 tonnes to be delivered by ship to the west coast of Mexico and 9,000 tonnes to be delivered by rail.
WHEAT TENDERS - A Philippine firm on Wednesday rejected offers on 40,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for delivery in March and April because of high prices, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association should tender Thursday for 69,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. Half is for March 15 to April 5 shipment from the Pacific Northwest (PNW), the rest for March 31 to April 20 from the PNW, traders said.

- The European Union was scheduled to tender February 25 to supply 45,000 tonnes of EU soft wheat as food aid to Bangladesh, France's grain office ONIC said. The EU will hold another tender that day to supply Ivory Coast with 2,480 tonnes of EU maize flour as food aid.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC seeks 10,500 tonnes US hard red wheat February 26 for Bangladesh. It seeks 5,870 tonnes of hard red winter wheat and 4,660 HRW or hard red spring for March 15-April 10 shipment.

MARKET TALK - China's corn exports could pick up as some South Korean and Asian buyers appear to be willing to pay more for the convenience of having small cargoes delivered to their smaller ports, Far East traders said.
-- Indonesian feed mills are believed to have locked in some 400,000 tonnes of mostly U.S. corn for delivery in the second quarter of 1997, traders said.
-- Egypt's main commodities buyer said the 400,000 tonnes of soft white Australian wheat Egypt had bought about a month ago from the Australian Wheat Board would be shipped in April and May.
-- Japan's Food Agency said on Wednesday it had agreed with the Australian Wheat Board to buy about 900,000 tonnes of wheat in calendar 1997.
-- Colombia's Agriculture Ministry said permits had been issued for the import of 140,000 tonnes of rough rice that will be shipped into the country May 15.

-- U.S. rice will likely be included when Colombia buys some or all of the 140,000 tonnes it has approved for import, U.S. exporters and traders said. "At least a portion of it will be U.S.," said one U.S. rice exporter, who expects Colombia to tender soon.

--USDA Wednesday said it raised Russia's GSM-102 credit guarantee line by $20 million to $70 million for fiscal year 1997. Earlier this month, USDA said Russia had expressed interest in buying U.S. wheat and/or wheat flour.
